api:
<TimeSeries> plots values over time: metrics, latency percentiles, request rates. It is a port of Grafana's Time series panel. It shares everything with <Trend>, which in Grafana is built on Time series too, and adds the time-specific options: a time axis by default, several timezones and time compare.

use blenderui::prelude::*;
use bui_charts::*;
  • <TimeSeries>
  • Time axis and timezones
  • Time compare
  • Coming from Grafana

Not sure which option fits? See the guide.

<TimeSeries>

<TimeSeries data={metrics} x={|m: &Metric| m.time} annotations={deploys}>
    <TrendSeries name="p99" y={|m: &Metric| m.p99} />
    <TrendSeries name="p50" y={|m: &Metric| m.p50} line_style={LineStyle::DASH} />
</TimeSeries>

Every prop of <Trend> works the same here. Series are <TrendSeries> tags, with the same style props, axes, stacking, colours and thresholds, missing values, annotations, exemplars and zoom and tooltip, legend and keyboard.

These props differ or are new:

PropTypeDefault
xFn(&T) -> f64: milliseconds since the Unix epochfor a Frame: the x_field, or the first field
x_axisAxisConfigAxisConfig::new().time(), in UTC
timezones&'static [i32]: UTC offsets in minutes[0]
time_comparef64: a shift in millisecondsnone

Time axis and timezones

The x axis is a time axis even when you pass your own x_axis. Tick labels pick a round step (seconds up to years) and show only what changes, as in Grafana.

timezones adds one row of tick labels per timezone, under the first, all at the same ticks. The first entry is the main axis and is also used in the tooltip:

timezones={&[0, 330, -300]}

shows UTC, UTC+5:30 and UTC−5. With orientation={VizOrientation::Vertical}, each timezone gets a column of labels instead.

Time compare

time_compare={24. * HOUR} draws every series a second time, shifted forward by that amount, so yesterday's values sit under today's. The copies:

  • are dashed, unfilled and never stacked, in the colour of their series;
  • are named "<name> (1d ago)", and show in the legend and tooltip like any series;
  • take each value from the row exactly one shift earlier, within half the smallest gap between rows. Rows without a match are left as gaps.

Your data must cover the earlier period too: to compare the last 24 hours with the 24 before, pass 48 hours of rows.

Coming from Grafana

Everything in Trend's table, plus:

Grafana optionHere
Time zone, additional time zonestimezones
Time shift / comparetime_compare
Orientationorientation
Annotations, Exemplarsannotations, exemplars
Disable keyboard eventskeyboard={false}

Not available here: the legend's faceted label filter (series here have no labels), dashboard time pickers and annotation editing.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Two series on a UTC time axis.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn basic() {
    let data = use_signal(metrics(120, MINUTE, 1));
    rsx! {
        <TimeSeries data={data} x={|m: &Metric| m.time} class="h-64">
            <TrendSeries name="CPU %" y={|m: &Metric| m.cpu} />
            <TrendSeries name="Memory %" y={|m: &Metric| m.memory} />
        </TimeSeries>
    }
}

examples.title: Annotations
examples.description: Deploy markers and an incident region; hover the markers at the bottom.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn deploys() {
    let data = use_signal(metrics(120, MINUTE, 2));
    let notes = vec![
        Annotation::at(T0 + 20. * MINUTE, "Deploy v1.4.2").text("Rolled out to 100% of pods"),
        Annotation::region(T0 + 55. * MINUTE, T0 + 75. * MINUTE, "Incident #218")
            .text("Elevated latency on checkout")
            .color(rgb(0xd20f39)),
        Annotation::at(T0 + 95. * MINUTE, "Deploy v1.4.3"),
    ];
    rsx! {
        <TimeSeries data={data} x={|m: &Metric| m.time} annotations={notes} class="h-64">
            <TrendSeries name="p99 ms" y={|m: &Metric| m.p99} />
        </TimeSeries>
    }
}

examples.title: Exemplars
examples.description: Individual slow requests as diamonds over the percentiles.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn exemplars() {
    let data = use_signal(metrics(120, MINUTE, 3));
    let slow: Vec<(f64, f64)> = (0..12u64)
        .map(|index| {
            let at = (noise(index + 50) * 119.).floor();
            (T0 + at * MINUTE, 300. + noise(index + 90) * 200.)
        })
        .collect();
    rsx! {
        <TimeSeries data={data} x={|m: &Metric| m.time} exemplars={slow} class="h-64">
            <TrendSeries name="p50 ms" y={|m: &Metric| m.p50} />
            <TrendSeries name="p99 ms" y={|m: &Metric| m.p99} />
        </TimeSeries>
    }
}

examples.title: Drag to zoom
examples.description: Drag across the time axis; double-click to zoom out.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn zoom() {
    let data = use_signal(metrics(240, MINUTE, 4));
    let picked = use_signal(SharedString::Borrowed(
        "Drag across the chart to zoom. Double-click to zoom out.",
    ));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-64">
            <div class="text-xs">{picked.get()}</div>
            <TimeSeries
                data={data}
                x={|m: &Metric| m.time}
                on_select={move |range: SelectedRange, _: &mut Window, _: &mut App| {
                    let minutes = (range.x.1 - range.x.0) / MINUTE;
                    picked.set(SharedString::from(format!("Zoomed to {minutes:.0} minutes")));
                }}
                class="flex-1"
            >
                <TrendSeries name="requests/min" y={|m: &Metric| m.requests} />
            </TimeSeries>
        </div>
    }
}

examples.title: Missing values
examples.description: A gap, and the same gap spanned.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn nulls() {
    let data = use_signal(
        metrics(120, MINUTE, 13)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|mut metric| {
                if (40.0..60.).contains(&((metric.time - T0) / MINUTE)) {
                    metric.cpu = f64::NAN;
                }
                metric
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! {
        <TimeSeries data={data} x={|m: &Metric| m.time} class="h-64">
            <TrendSeries name="gap" y={|m: &Metric| m.cpu} />
            <TrendSeries name="spanned" y={|m: &Metric| m.cpu + 30.} span_nulls={NullSpan::Always} line_style={LineStyle::DASH} />
        </TimeSeries>
    }
}

examples.title: Live data
examples.description: A signal as data, a multi tooltip and a table legend.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live() {
    let round = use_signal(1u64);
    let data = use_signal(metrics(120, MINUTE, 1));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-64">
            <div
                id="next"
                class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline"
                onClick={move || {
                    let next = round.get() + 1;
                    round.set(next);
                    data.set(metrics(120, MINUTE, next));
                }}
            >
                "Load new data"
            </div>
            <TimeSeries data={data} x={|m: &Metric| m.time} tooltip={Tooltip::multi()} legend={Legend::table().calcs([Calc::Mean, Calc::Max])} class="flex-1">
                <TrendSeries name="p50 ms" y={|m: &Metric| m.p50} />
                <TrendSeries name="p99 ms" y={|m: &Metric| m.p99} />
            </TimeSeries>
        </div>
    }
}
